Welcome to your knowledge guide

This is a sample page shipped with the Knowledge Guide module. You can edit it, archive it, or remove it once you start building your own documentation.

What can you do here?

  • Organize documentation pages by collapsible categories
  • Restrict pages to specific user groups
  • Group pages into Books and publish them on a public URL
  • Track visits using Odoo's native link tracker
  • Send a guide by email to one or several recipients
Tip: Use the search bar at the top to quickly find a specific section of your guide.

Navigation

The guide is organized in three main areas:

Sidebar

The left-hand sidebar lists all pages grouped by category. Click on a category title to expand or collapse it.

Search

Use the search box at the top to filter pages in real time. Matches are highlighted in titles and content.

Reading area

The current page is displayed in the central reading area. Each page can contain rich HTML content (text, lists, tables, images, alerts, etc.).

Tip: When a guide is published as a Book, visitors get an additional Previous/Next pagination at the bottom of each page.

Override module-provided pages

When a page is shipped by another module, its Original content is read-only and stays in sync with the source module's data file.

If you need to adapt the wording for your own clients without losing the original, fill the Custom content field on the page form. The custom version is shown to readers, while the original stays available as a fallback.

Need to inspect the raw HTML of an original page? The View HTML source button on the page form opens a read-only viewer showing the unmodified markup.

Add your own pages

Any Odoo module can contribute its own documentation pages by depending on knowledge_guide and shipping an XML data file.

Example

<record id="page_my_module" model="knowledge.guide.page">
    <field name="name">My Feature</field>
    <field name="category">My Module</field>
    <field name="sequence">10</field>
    <field name="icon">fa-cog</field>
    <field name="module_source">my_module</field>
    <field name="content_html"><![CDATA[
        <h1>My Feature</h1>
        <p>Description...</p>
    ]]></field>
</record>

Then declare the file in your manifest:

'depends': ['knowledge_guide'],
'data': [
    'data/my_module_guide_data.xml',
],
